## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Cloth
//
// Bodies for the cloth vocabulary: the deformable types of
// `particles.types.plato` (`ClothVertex`, `ClothDistanceConstraint`,
// `ClothBendConstraint`, `Cloth3D`) and the builders and settings of
// `cloth.types.plato`.
//
// Cloth is the smallest simulation that shows the whole pipeline: a mesh
// becomes a constraint graph, the graph is solved, the solution becomes a mesh
// again. Both solvers here run over the SAME graph and the SAME integrator; the
// only thing that differs is where the constraint response enters — as a
// Hookean force before integration (mass-spring) or as a position correction
// after it (position-based dynamics).
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Cloth vertices — state and the integrator
//  - Rewriting the vertex array — the seam purity is paid at
//  - Distance constraints — projection and the Gauss-Seidel sweep
//  - Bend constraints — the dihedral projection
//  - Collision — sphere, plane, and any signed distance field
//  - Building a cloth — from a grid
//  - Building a cloth — from a polygon mesh
//  - The position-based solver
//  - The mass-spring solver
//  - Reading the result back

library Cloth
{
    //==
    // # Cloth vertices — state and the integrator
    //
    // Integrator: POSITION VERLET (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verlet_integration),
    // over the state `ClothVertex` already declares — a position and the
    // position at the previous step. Velocity is never stored; it is the
    // difference between the two, divided by the step.
    //
    // That choice is not arbitrary, and it is what lets one integrator serve
    // both solvers:
    //
    //  - Position-based dynamics needs exactly this pair anyway. Its velocity
    //    update after a solve is (corrected position - position before the
    //    step) / dt, which IS the Verlet difference quotient. Storing a
    //    velocity as well would mean keeping two answers to the same question.
    //  - Every response in this file is expressed by MOVING A POSITION —
    //    pinning, constraint projection, contact. With Verlet each of those
    //    produces the right velocity for free, because the previous position
    //    stays where it was. With a stored velocity each would need a second,
    //    separate edit, and forgetting one is the classic source of cloth that
    //    sticks to a collider or gains energy at a pin.
    //
    // `Particle3D` stores a velocity instead and is integrated with
    // semi-implicit Euler (`particles.library.plato`); the two states exist
    // because the two vocabularies genuinely want different things.

    // The vertex's implicit velocity over a step of `dt`: the difference
    // quotient of the two stored positions, in meters per second.
    Velocity(self: ClothVertex, dt: Duration): Vector3D
        => (self.Position - self.PreviousPosition) / dt.Seconds;

    // True when the vertex must not move: explicitly pinned, or of infinite
    // mass (a non-positive inverse mass).
    IsFixed(self: ClothVertex): Boolean
        => self.Pinned.Or(self.InverseMass <= 0.0);

    // The inverse mass the solvers actually divide corrections by: zero for a
    // fixed vertex. Every projection below reads this instead of testing the
    // pin flag, so pinning is a mass of infinity and nothing more.
    SolverInverseMass(self: ClothVertex): Number
        => self.IsFixed ? 0.0 : self.InverseMass;

    // The same vertex placed at a new position, with the previous position,
    // mass and pin flag untouched. Moving the position alone is how a
    // correction becomes a velocity change: the difference quotient picks it up
    // on the next step, which is the response position-based dynamics wants
    // from both a constraint and a contact.
    MovedTo(self: ClothVertex, position: Point3D): ClothVertex
        => ClothVertex(position, self.PreviousPosition, self.InverseMass, self.Pinned);

    // The same vertex displaced by `delta`, or unchanged when it is fixed.
    Displaced(self: ClothVertex, delta: Vector3D): ClothVertex
        => self.IsFixed ? self : self.MovedTo(self.Position + delta);

    // The same vertex pinned or released. A vertex pinned mid-simulation keeps
    // whatever velocity it had until the next `Integrate` collapses it.
    WithPinned(self: ClothVertex, pinned: Boolean): ClothVertex
        => ClothVertex(self.Position, self.PreviousPosition, self.InverseMass, pinned);

    // One position-Verlet update: the next position is the current one, plus
    // the implicit velocity decayed by `damping`, plus the acceleration term
    // a * dt^2. The current position becomes the previous one.
    //
    // A fixed vertex is collapsed onto itself — both positions set to the
    // current one — so a vertex pinned part-way through a simulation stops dead
    // rather than continuing to carry the velocity it had.
    Integrate(self: ClothVertex, acceleration: Vector3D, dt: Duration, damping: Number): ClothVertex
        => self.IsFixed
            ? ClothVertex(self.Position, self.Position, self.InverseMass, self.Pinned)
            : ClothVertex(
                self.Position
                    + (self.Position - self.PreviousPosition) * (1.0 - damping)
                    + acceleration * (dt.Seconds * dt.Seconds),
                self.Position,
                self.InverseMass,
                self.Pinned);

    //==
    // # Rewriting the vertex array — the seam purity is paid at
    //
    // Constraint projection is naturally in-place: a solver writes two vertices
    // and moves on. Plato has no in-place write to an `Array`, so each
    // projection below returns a NEW vertex array with the touched entries
    // replaced, built by a single `MapRange` over the old one.
    //
    // That is the whole cost of doing this purely, and it is worth stating
    // plainly: one projection is O(vertex count) rather than O(1), so one
    // Gauss-Seidel sweep is O(vertices * constraints) where the in-place
    // version is O(constraints). Nothing else about the algorithm changes —
    // the arithmetic, the convergence and the results are identical.
    //
    // The affine builder `Buffer<ClothVertex>` (`primitives.plato`) would give
    // the in-place cost back and stay pure by uniqueness, but it cannot drive
    // this loop: a builder may not be captured in a lambda or used as a generic
    // argument (LINT006 / LINT007), and Plato has no loop form, so there is no
    // way to sweep a constraint array over one. See the sweep section below for
    // the alternative that IS available.

    // The vertex array with one vertex replaced.
    WithVertex(self: Array<ClothVertex>, index: VertexIndex, vertex: ClothVertex): Array<ClothVertex>
        => self.Count.MapRange(i => i == index.Value ? vertex : self[i]);

    // The vertex array with a distance constraint's two ends replaced, in one
    // rebuild rather than two.
    WithTwoVertices(self: Array<ClothVertex>, c: ClothDistanceConstraint, a: ClothVertex, b: ClothVertex): Array<ClothVertex>
        => self.Count.MapRange(i =>
            i == c.VertexA.Value ? a
            : (i == c.VertexB.Value ? b : self[i]));

    // The vertex array with a bend constraint's four vertices replaced, in one
    // rebuild rather than four.
    WithFourVertices(self: Array<ClothVertex>, c: ClothBendConstraint, a: ClothVertex, b: ClothVertex, wingC: ClothVertex, wingD: ClothVertex)
        : Array<ClothVertex>
        => self.Count.MapRange(i =>
            i == c.VertexA.Value ? a
            : (i == c.VertexB.Value ? b
            : (i == c.VertexC.Value ? wingC
            : (i == c.VertexD.Value ? wingD : self[i]))));

    // The cloth with a new vertex array; constraints, faces and thickness are
    // shared unchanged, which is what makes a step cheap in everything but the
    // positions.
    WithVertices(self: Cloth3D, vertices: Array<ClothVertex>): Cloth3D
        => Cloth3D(vertices, self.DistanceConstraints, self.BendConstraints, self.Faces, self.Thickness);
```
